questions.enonce_markdown:
Find the values of $R$ and $\alpha$, $R > 0$ and $0^\circ < \alpha < 90^\circ$, for which

$$4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta \equiv R\cos(\theta - \alpha).$$

Hence, obtain the greatest value of the expression $\dfrac{1}{4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta + 6}$, and give the corresponding value of $\theta$ between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Harmonic form.** Expand: $R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = R\cos\alpha\cos\theta + R\sin\alpha\sin\theta$. Compare coefficients with $4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta$:

$$R\cos\alpha = 4, \qquad R\sin\alpha = 3.$$

Squaring and adding: $R^2 = 16 + 9 = 25$, so $R = 5$ (as $R > 0$). Dividing: $\tan\alpha = \dfrac34$, and since $\cos\alpha > 0$, $\sin\alpha > 0$ ($\alpha$ acute),

$$\boxed{R = 5, \qquad \alpha = \tan^{-1}\tfrac34 = 36.87^\circ \;(36.9^\circ \text{ to 1 d.p.})}$$

**Greatest value.** The expression becomes

$$\frac{1}{4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta + 6} = \frac{1}{5\cos(\theta - \alpha) + 6}.$$

Since $-1 \le \cos(\theta - \alpha) \le 1$, the denominator $5\cos(\theta - \alpha) + 6$ lies between $1$ and $11$, so it is always positive and the expression is always defined. The fraction is greatest when the (positive) denominator is smallest, that is when $\cos(\theta - \alpha) = -1$, where the denominator equals $5(-1) + 6 = 1$:

$$\boxed{\text{greatest value} = 1}$$

This occurs when $\theta - \alpha = 180^\circ$, so $\theta = 180^\circ + 36.87^\circ$:

$$\boxed{\theta = 216.87^\circ \;(\approx 216.9^\circ)}$$

Check: $4\cos 216.87^\circ + 3\sin 216.87^\circ = 4(-0.8) + 3(-0.6) = -5$, and $-5 + 6 = 1$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using De Moivre's theorem, write down the equivalent form of $\cos 3\theta + i\sin 3\theta$.

Hence show that $\sin 3\theta \equiv 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**De Moivre's theorem:** for any integer $n$, $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^n = \cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta$. With $n = 3$:

$$\cos 3\theta + i\sin 3\theta = (\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^3.$$

**Expand** the right-hand side with the binomial theorem, using $i^2 = -1$ and $i^3 = -i$:

$$(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^3 = \cos^3\theta + 3\cos^2\theta\,(i\sin\theta) + 3\cos\theta\,(i\sin\theta)^2 + (i\sin\theta)^3$$

$$= \left(\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta\right) + i\left(3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta - \sin^3\theta\right).$$

**Equate imaginary parts** (the real and imaginary parts of two equal complex numbers are equal, for real $\theta$):

$$\sin 3\theta = 3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta - \sin^3\theta.$$

Use $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$:

$$\sin 3\theta = 3(1 - \sin^2\theta)\sin\theta - \sin^3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 3\sin^3\theta - \sin^3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta.$$

$$\boxed{\sin 3\theta \equiv 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta} \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Equating real parts similarly gives $\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$. Quick check at $\theta = 30^\circ$: $\sin 90^\circ = 1$ and $3(0.5) - 4(0.125) = 1$.)
